must_read.title: Impact of Body Mass Index on Treatment Outcomes in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer Patients Treated With Definitive Chemoradiotherapy or Radiotherapy Alone
must_read.title_zh: 体重指数对局部晚期头颈部癌根治性放化疗或单纯放疗疗效的影响
must_read.one_line: 回顾性队列：BMI<25kg/m²患者放化疗后毒性更高、OS更低，BMI为独立预后因素。
must_read.so_what: 营养-免疫代谢关联，提示q5中肿瘤微环境营养状态可调，但无分子机制。
must_read.caution: 单中心回顾性，BMI为营养代理指标，混杂因素多，因果力弱。
must_read.abstract: BACKGROUND: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a readily measured indicator of nutritional status; however, its impact on outcomes in head and neck cancer (HNC) patients remains understudied. This study evaluated the impact of pre-treatment BMI on toxicities and survival in such patients. METHODS: This retrospective study included 212 patients of locally advanced HNC treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone. Patients were categorized into BMI < 25 kg/m2 and ≥ 25 kg/m2. Toxicities were assessed using CTCAE v5.0. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional control (LRC) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Eighty-six percent of patients had BMI of < 25Kg/m2. These patients experienced significantly higher rates of grade ≥ 2 mucositis, dermatitis, candidiasis, and greater need for nutritional support (44.7%; p = 0.039). Median OS and LRC were 25 and 24 months, respectively. Three-year OS and LRC were 46.3% and 39%. BMI category, T stage, and nodal stage independently predicted OS. CONCLUSION: BMI < 25 Kg/m2 patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone are more prone to treatment-related toxicities and have inferior survival outcomes. Early nutritional assessment and intervention should be integrated into routine management to improve treatment outcomes.

deep.title_zh: 体重指数对局部晚期头颈部癌根治性放化疗或单纯放疗疗效的影响
deep.one_sentence: BMI<25kg/m2的局部晚期HNC患者接受根治性放化疗/单纯放疗后，毒性反应更高、生存更差；BMI是OS的独立预测…
deep.question: 在根治性放化疗或单纯放疗的局部晚期头颈部癌患者中，低BMI（<25kg/m2）是否通过影响治疗耐受性和抗肿瘤免疫微环境，进而降低生存获益？
deep.design: 回顾性单中心队列研究，按BMI<25 vs ≥25分组，比较放化疗/单纯放疗患者的急性毒性（CTCAE v5.0）与OS、LRC；多变量Cox分析校正T/N分期。
deep.sample_desc: 212例局部晚期头颈部癌患者，接受根治性同步放化疗或单纯放疗；摘要未说明医院/地区来源。

findings.claim: BMI<25患者更常发生≥2级黏膜炎、皮炎、念珠菌病，营养支持需求更高。

findings.evidence: 中位OS 25月、LRC 24月；3年OS 46.3%、3年LRC 39%。BMI为OS独立预测因子（与T分期、N分期并列）。

findings.claim: BMI在HNC放化疗人群中独立于TN分期预测生存。
findings.evidence: 多变量Cox回归显示BMI分类、T分期、N分期均独立预测OS。

deep.relation: 与q5（口腔鳞癌的免疫微环境与微生物组如何共同塑造治疗抵抗？有无可转化的干预点？）相关，提供新解释：低BMI/营养不良状态可能是'治疗抵抗'的外周驱动因素——通过增加急性毒性、迫使治疗中断或剂量削减，间接降低肿瘤控制率；营养支持可能是可转化的干预点。与q2的'宿主代谢-肿瘤'轴亦有交叉。
deep.why: 大多数HNC预后研究聚焦于HPV状态、基因突变或肿瘤微环境；本研究以'可操作的临床指标'BMI为切入点，证实营养状态是OS独立预测因子，并直接给出'早期营养评估+干预应纳入常规管理'的临床转化路径。对做头颈肿瘤/口腔鳞癌免疫微环境课题的研究者，提示：不应忽略患者的代谢-营养背景对治疗反应和免疫微环境的系统性调制作用。
limitations: 回顾性单中心设计，BMI仅采用单一截断值（25kg/m2），无法捕捉剂量-反应关系或非线性效应；也未报告BMI变化轨迹（治疗前后）。
未校正合并症（如糖尿病、心血管疾病）、吸烟史、饮酒史、KPS评分、ALB/前白蛋白等营养/炎症指标，存在残余混杂；'独立预测'结论需谨慎。
未区分原发部位（口咽 vs 非口咽），而口咽癌HPV状态与预后密切相关，混合入组可能掩盖异质性。
deep.transferable: （1）将'营养风险筛查（NRS-2002或PG-SGA）'与'放化疗毒性预测'联合设计，纳入自己的HNC免疫微环境课题；（2）若做口腔鳞癌类器官/器官芯片，可模拟营养不良状态（低葡萄糖/低氨基酸）与免疫细胞共培养，观察对放化疗敏感性的影响；（3）用孟德尔随机化检验BMI与HNC放化疗毒性/预后的因果方向，弥补回顾性研…
followups: 原始数据是否报告了BMI各等级（如<18.5、18.5–24.9、25–29.9、≥30）的剂量-反应趋势？截断值25是否来自预设还是数据驱动？
多变量Cox模型的HR及95%CI是多少？模型是否经过比例风险假设检验？
研究是否报告了放化疗中断率、剂量削减率与BMI的关系？毒性升高是否中介了生存差异？

must_reads.title: Artificial Intelligence in Dental Research: Innovation versus Integrity?
must_reads.title_zh: 人工智能在牙科研究中的创新与诚信挑战
must_reads.one_line: 探讨LLM与智能体管道重塑口腔研究知识生产的机遇与风险
must_reads.so_what: 提醒AI辅助写作/分析的诚信边界，可迁移到多组学数据分析流程设计
must_reads.caution: 观点性文章无原创数据，引用需独立核实
must_reads.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models and agentic pipelines, is reshaping dental research. This article examines the opportunities and risks of AI in knowledge production in oral health research. On one hand, AI accelerates literature synthesis, data analysis, and manuscript drafting; on the other, it introduces new risks, including fabricated findings and citations, overconfident inference, and homogenization of research focus. These shifts challenge the mechanisms that maintain scientific credibility such as peer review, reproducibility, and human judgment, especially in fields like dentistry, where small datasets and limited editorial capacity may amplify vulnerabilities. We here identify 3 structural asymmetries: 1) the growing gap between the rapid pace of AI-assisted production and slow human validation, 2) the divergence between AI-generated linguistic fluency and the true robustness of the generated evidence, and 3) unequal institutional capacity to govern AI and the incentives set by the research system for (mis)using AI for research. We conclude with a call for proportional and enforceable governance frameworks, including mandatory AI disclosure standards, provenance tracking, structured adversarial testing of research tools, and interdisciplinary oversight. Moreover, we suggest institutional reform, including revising incentive structures, fostering AI literacy, and enforcing auditability to safeguard research integrity. In the age of machine-assisted content, credibility becomes a scarce resource. Dental science must not merely adopt AI but actively govern it to ensure that its accelerated outputs remain trustworthy, equitable, and clinically meaningful.

scan.title: Generative AI in Endodontics: A Scoping Review of Applications, Performance, and Limitations
scan.title_zh: 生成式AI在牙体牙髓的应用范围综述
scan.one_line: 范围综述汇总50项研究，生成式AI主要用于牙体牙髓教育、诊断支持和患者沟通。
scan.so_what: 可了解AI工具边界，不涉机制
scan.caution: 纳入大量case report/技术说明
scan.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has been increasingly studied and applied in endodontics, offering accessible tools for clinical decision support, education, and patient communication without requiring advanced technical expertise. This scoping review aimed to map current applications of LLM-based generative AI in endodontics and to synthesize evidence on their performance, limitations, and key evidence gaps. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search using a predefined Boolean search strategy was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection for studies published between January 1, 2023 and November 19, 2025. English-language studies evaluating LLM-based generative AI applications in endodontics were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers and synthesized to identify applications, key outcomes, and limitations. RESULTS: A total of 50 studies were included. Applications were categorized into education and training (n = 20), diagnosis and clinical support (n = 21), and patient communication (n = 9). GPT-series models via ChatGPT were the most frequently assessed. In education, LLMs demonstrated high accuracy in structured multiple-choice assessments, but showed lower performance in open-ended and case-based tasks; in the four studies that included human comparators, LLMs outperformed students in two and fell below human examinees in two. In diagnostic and clinical decision-making contexts, performance was promising, but inconsistent, with improvements being observed when structured clinical input was provided, yet remaining below expert-level performance. In patient communication, LLMs were associated with improved patient ratings and engagement, but revealed a trade-off between accuracy, readability, and completeness. CONCLUSIONS: This review shows the potential of LLM-based generative AI in endodontics; however, its performance is strongly affected by task type and both model- and implementation-related factors. Therefore, the development of standardized, prospectively validated evaluation frameworks is important for supporting a reliable assessment and is expected to facilitate the safe and effective integration of generative AI into clinical and educational practice.

scan.title: Oral Aspects in Adolescents Born Extremely Preterm: Results From the National Swedish Cohort Study
scan.title_zh: 极早产青少年口腔健康全国性队列研究
scan.one_line: 横断面电话调查比较<27周早产与足月青少年TMD疼痛、正畸需求及口腔行为差异
scan.caution: 横断面设计，问卷主诉，无法推断因果
scan.abstract: BACKGROUND: Taking a holistic approach to the health outcomes of extremely preterm (EPT) adolescents, where oral health is a part of general health, is important to ensure lifelong wellbeing. OBJECTIVE: This interdisciplinary cross-sectional survey investigated oral health aspects, including temporomandibular disorders (TMD) pain, desire for orthodontic treatment, dental fear and anxiety (DFA), and oral health behaviour in adolescents born before 27 weeks of gestation. Comparisons were made with term-born controls (≥ 37 weeks of gestation). METHODS: Structured telephone interviews were conducted with adolescents and their parents. The questionnaire included validated screening questions on TMD pain and DFA, as well as questions on subjective orthodontic treatment need and oral health behaviour. Group comparisons were performed using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression analyses were used to estimate crude and adjusted odds ratios (ORs), controlling for sex, age, and dental fear. RESULTS: A total of 198 EPT adolescents (mean age 15.8) and 152 controls (mean age 15.7) participated. The odds of reporting TMD pain were 2.43 times higher in the EPT group than in controls (p = 0.002), and the odds of reporting a desire for orthodontic treatment were 3.48 times higher (p = 0.001). Additionally, the EPT group showed significantly higher Children's Fear Survey Schedule-Dental Subscale (CFSS-DS) scores, indicating higher DFA and less stable toothbrushing habits than controls. CONCLUSION: EPT adolescents showed a less favourable oral health profile than controls. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness in dental care, tailored preventive interventions, and support during the transition to adult healthcare to promote lifelong oral health and wellbeing.

scan.title: Direct Oral Healthcare Costs Associated With Xerostomia and Hyposalivation: A Scoping Review and Annual Cost Synthesis
scan.title_zh: 口干症直接口腔医疗成本的范围综述
scan.one_line: 范围综述汇总8项研究估算口干症相关直接口腔医疗成本，证据异质性高
scan.caution: 异质性大，成本估算基于假设频率，临床转化弱
scan.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To map the available evidence on direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia and hyposalivation. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science, with additional screening of gray literature. Studies reporting direct oral healthcare costs associated with xerostomia or/and hyposalivation were eligible. Reported costs were standardized to a common currency and price year. Exploratory annual cost scenarios were generated by combining reported unit costs with reported guideline-based or hypothetical frequencies. RESULTS: Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Six (75%) were conducted in the United States and two (25%) in the United Kingdom. Reported cost components included dental consultations, salivary stimulants and substitutes, restorative treatments, dental implants, fluoride applications, and management of oral infections. Evidence was heterogeneous in populations, etiologies, healthcare settings, cost components, and reporting methods. Illustrative base-case scenarios ranged from USD 3296.08 to USD 10,414.51 per patient per year (USD 1791.23-5658.99 when hypothetical events and possible overlaps were excluded). CONCLUSION: The evidence base is limited and heterogeneous. The exploratory annual synthesis provides an initial framework for mapping reported cost components but does not represent a definitive estimate of economic burden.

scan.title: Outcomes Following Extreme Elective Nodal De-Escalation in HNSCC Treated With Curative Intent: A Community Program Experience
scan.title_zh: 超选择性淋巴结降剂量放疗在HNSCC中的应用
scan.domain: 牙周炎通过哪些可验证的通…
scan.one_line: 大样本回顾：30-40Gy超选择性淋巴结降剂量放疗未增加复发风险，疗效可控。
scan.so_what: 涉及治疗抵抗场景，但为临床技术描述，无免疫/微生物机制，q5转化价值有限。
scan.caution: 单中心回顾性大样本，选择偏倚难消除，非RCT证据。
scan.abstract: PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE(S): To evaluate elective nodal recurrence rates in HNSCC patients treated with extreme dose de-escalation to 30 or 40 Gy followed by a sequential boost to gross disease or high-risk sites. MATERIALS/METHODS: Between May 2017 and May 2025, patients diagnosed with SCC of the oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx were treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or surgery followed by adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy. Elective nodal volumes (ENV) defined as any uninvolved adjacent, distant ipsilateral or contralateral anatomic nodal level were treated to either 30 or 40 Gy, followed by a sequential boost to the PTVp/PTVn+ or high-risk surgical bed (PTVp+ PTVn+). A subset of 6 patients received 24-36 Gy (1.5-1.8 Gy BID) based on the Mayo-DART regimen. Assignment to 40 Gy versus 30 Gy reflected the radiation oncologist preference based on emerging trial evidence. All cases were reviewed prospectively in a head and neck multidisciplinary conference, and treatment planning required diagnostic FDG PET-CT fused to the planning CT. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 99% of patients. The primary endpoint was regional failure rate within the de-escalated ENV. Secondary endpoints included 1- and 2-year locoregional control (LRC), progression-free survival (PFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), and failure patterns. RESULTS: The analysis included 102 patients of whom the majority 81.4% received definitive chemoradiotherapy, 17.6% underwent surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and 1% received surgery with adjuvant radiation alone. The elective nodal volume was treated to 40 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 81 patients and to 30 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 15 patients; the remaining 6 adjuvant patients received 24-36 Gy at 1.5-1.8 Gy twice daily per the Mayo-DART regimen. With a median follow-up of 26.4 months, no elective nodal failures were observed in either dose cohort. The 1- and 2-year LRC rates were 93.5%. The 1- and 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 88.6% and 87.3%, respectively, while distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) rates were 95.0% and 95.0%, respectively. In total, 13 recurrences were recorded comprising 7 locoregional and 6 distant failures. CONCLUSION: This represents the largest report demonstrating the efficacy of extreme dose de-escalation to ENV's for HNSCC within an NCI designated community cancer program.

scan.title: A Split-Mouth Randomised Controlled Clinical Trial: Comparing Ostectomy Performed With Piezosurgery Versus Burs for Aesthetic Crown-Lengthening Surgery
scan.title_zh: 超声骨刀vs手机冠延长术RCT
scan.one_line: 半口RCT：超声骨刀与高速手机行美容性冠延长术，6个月牙龈边缘及骨改建无显著差异。
scan.so_what: 纯技术对比，不涉及免疫微环境或骨结合机制，仅背景。
scan.caution: n=15极小，半口设计虽控偏但外展推广需谨慎。
scan.abstract: AIM: To assess the clinical, profilometric, radiographic and patient-reported outcomes following aesthetic crown lengthening (ECL) with ostectomy performed using either piezosurgery (PS) or rotary burs (RB). METHODS: Fifteen patients with altered passive eruption underwent ECL from maxillary premolar to premolar in a 6-month split-mouth randomised design. Ostectomy was performed with either PS or RB. Clinical, profilometric and radiographic assessments, as well as patient-reported outcomes, were collected. The primary outcome was the change in gingival margin (GM) position between 6 weeks and 6 months, analysed with a linear mixed model with treatment as a fixed effect and patient as a random effect. RESULTS: Between 6 weeks and 6 months (primary outcome), GM change was 0.16 ± 0.19 mm in the PS group and 0.12 ± 0.21 mm in the RB group (p = 0.170). The greatest reduction in crown height occurred between suturing and 7 days (-0.63 ± 0.35 mm). CEJ-BC remodelling from surgery to 6 months was -0.22 ± 0.42 mm (PS) and -0.26 ± 0.44 mm (RB) (p = 0.491). CONCLUSION: PS and RB showed no significant difference in GM stability following ECL, with the greatest changes in the first week and stability by 6 weeks.

scan.title: The Association Between Muscle Health and Quality of Life in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Systematic Review
scan.title_zh: 头颈癌肌肉健康与QoL系统评价
scan.one_line: 系统评价：较差肌肉健康与HNC患者QoL多个维度下降相关，但证据不支持meta分析。
scan.so_what: 综述确认关联，但缺乏因果推断，q5关注的是免疫机制而非功能结局。
scan.caution: 纳入研究异质性高，QUINS工具评估主观性强，结论为弱关联。
scan.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) are at risk of impaired muscle health due to metabolic disturbances, reduced nutritional intake, and treatment-related toxicities. Because muscle health supports physical capacity and independence, its decline may affect quality of life (QoL). This systematic review examined the association between muscle health and QoL in patients with HNC. METHODS: Studies were included if they involved patients with HNC, used validated muscle health and QoL measures, and examined their association. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool. RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. Poorer muscle health was associated with lower global QoL, poorer physical and role functioning, greater fatigue, swallowing difficulties, restricted mouth opening, social eating problems, and salivary toxicities. Methodological limitations and heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Poorer muscle health was associated with worse QoL in patients with HNC, although this evidence does not establish causality. Prospective studies using standardized measures are needed. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO Number: CRD42025105208.

scan.title: Effector-triggered stomatal immunity prevents leaf invasion by bacterial pathogens
scan.title_zh: 效应因子触发气孔免疫阻止细菌入侵
scan.one_line: 拟南芥CAR1受体识别P.syringae AvrE1效应蛋白，延长气孔免疫关闭时间
scan.caution: 植物模型，免疫机制与人类口腔免疫差异巨大
scan.abstract: The phytopathogen Pseudomonas syringae must enter the leaf interior through natural openings such as stomata to cause disease. Plants restrict pathogen entry into the leaf through non-self-recognition-driven stomatal closure. P. syringae counters this stomatal immunity by deploying a range of toxins and effectors. Here, we show that stomatal immunity in Arabidopsis thaliana is reinforced upon recognition of the ubiquitous P. syringae type III effector AvrE1 by the resistance protein CAR1. CAR1 expression is enriched in guard cells, and its activation prolongs the effective duration of stomatal immunity. We also show that CAR1 prevents the invasion of leaf tissue by natural isolates of P. syringae, demonstrating that stomatal immunity provides a broadly significant barrier to host accessibility by P. syringae that carry the conserved effector AvrE1.
